workflow: Multiple threads concurrently read and update shared process-wide locale state without synchronization.
One thread obtains a pointer to dynamically allocated locale text while another thread replaces the locale and releases the old text.
The first thread continues decoding or measuring the text through the stale pointer after its backing storage has been freed.
The concurrent use-after-free is detected and the process terminates instead of safely serializing the updates.
summary: Concurrent shared locale-state replacement causes use-after-free
decision_reason: The failure is materially the same as unsynchronized mutation of shared native state during concurrent use: one thread invalidates shared backing storage while another thread still uses it. The locale-specific details are incidental.
